'''Alessandra Lunardi''' (born 1958){{r|born}} is an Italian mathematician specializing in [[mathematical analysis]]. She is a professor in the department of mathematics and computer science at the [[University of Parma]].{{r|profile}} She is particularly interested in [[Kolmogorov equations]] and  [[Free boundary problem|free boundary problems]].{{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Lunardi was educated at the [[University of Pisa]], completing her undergraduate studies there in 1980 and earning a Ph.D. there in 1983.{{r|profile}} Her dissertation, ''Analyticity of the maximal solution to fully nonlinear equations in Banach spaces'', was supervised by Giuseppe Da Prato.{{r|mg}}

After continuing on at Pisa as a researcher from 1984 to 1987, she was hired as a full professor at the [[University of Cagliari]] in 1987, and moved to Parma in 1994.{{r|profile}}

==Contributions==
Lunardi is the author of ''Analytic semigroups and optimal regularity in parabolic problems'' ([[Birkhäuser]], 1995, reprinted 2013){{r|asor}} and of ''Interpolation theory'' (Edizioni della Normale, 1998, 3rd ed., 2018).{{r|it}} With [[Giuseppe Da Prato|G. Da Prato]], P. C. Kunstmann, [[Irena Lasiecka|I. Lasiecka]], R. Schnaubelt, and L. Weis, she is a co-author of ''Functional Analytic Methods for Evolution Equations'' (Springer, 2004).

Lunardi is one of six [[Editor-in-chief|editors-in-chief]] of the journal ''Nonlinear Differential Equations and Applications (NoDEA)''.{{r|nodea}} She also served as editor-in-chief of ''[[Rivista di Matematica della Università di Parma]]'' for Series 7 of the journal, from 2002 to 2008.{{r|rev}}

==Recognition==
In 1987, Lunardi won the [[Bartolozzi Prize]] of the [[Italian Mathematical Union]].{{r|profile}} In 2017, she won the {{ill|Lucio & Wanda Amerio Gold Medal Prize|it|Premio Amerio}} of the [[Istituto Lombardo Accademia di Scienze e Lettere]].{{r|amerio}}
